h1: The 6 Best Hose Reel Carts Under $150, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Hose Reel Carts Under $150: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 hose reel carts for $150 or less, compared on hose capacity, wheels, brass fittings, crank design and frame material.
summary: The WERMAH 300 ft cart is the best hose reel cart under $150, with 10 inch airless tires and a one-piece brass connector. Real Hose Storage has the best crank, Poakkus is the value pick with 300 ft and brass fittings, and GrillTown is the pre-assembled choice for small yards.
intro: Most hose reel carts fail at the same three places: the connector leaks, the wheels flatten or the cart tips when you pull the hose. Capacity is the headline number on every listing, but these three details decide whether you keep the cart or send it back. A 300 ft cart that tips on its first pull is worse than a 175 ft one that rolls true.

We ranked six carts by capacity, wheel design, connectors, crank and frame, using listing data and maker specs. Prices in the listing data span $50 to $200, so check each current price against your $150 ceiling before you buy. One VEVOR listing contradicts itself on wheel count, and we flag it where it counts, in the ranking.

products.name: WERMAH 4-Wheel Hose Reel Cart 300 ft
products.verdict: 300 ft capacity, 10 inch airless tires and a one-piece angled brass connector.
products.description:
WERMAH's cart swallows 300 ft of 5/8 inch hose and rolls on four non-slip airless tires that measure 10 inches across. It has a one-piece angled brass connector with precision seals, a 6.5 ft leader hose and a storage basket. It sits in the $100 to $200 range.

The connector is the part that decides whether a hose reel leaks. A one-piece angled brass fitting removes the seam where cheap reels drip and kink the leader. Airless tires never go flat, and four 10 inch wheels let the cart roll over roots and gravel without tipping when you pull.

Buy it for a large yard with long runs. It lands at the top of the budget and may exceed $150 on some listings, so check the current price against your ceiling.
products.idealFor: Large yards with long hose runs.
products.skipIf: The listing price exceeds your cap.

products.name: Real Hose Storage 4-Wheel Hose Reel Cart 250 ft
products.verdict: A comfortable padded crank on a rust-resistant powder-coated steel frame.
products.description:
Real Hose Storage's cart holds 250 ft of 5/8 inch hose on four airless tires, with a crank labeled E-Z Ergo whose grip is wrapped in foam, a rust-resistant steel frame with powder coat, and a 6 ft leader hose. It sits in the $100 to $200 bracket.

Winding 250 ft of wet hose is a workout, and the crank decides whether it hurts. A padded ergonomic handle spreads the load across your palm. It trails the WERMAH by 50 ft of capacity and a seamless connector.

Buy it for a mid-size yard where you wind often. The listing does not name the connector material, so check it.
products.idealFor: Frequent winders who want a comfortable crank.

products.name: Poakkus 300 ft 4-Wheel Hose Reel Cart
products.verdict: 300 ft capacity, 10 inch PU wheels and brass fittings in the $50 to $100 range.
products.description:
Poakkus makes a 300 ft capacity cart with four 10 inch polyurethane wheels, a powder-coated steel frame, brass fittings, an ergonomic non-slip crank and a built-in storage basket. It sells for $50 to $100.

It offers the 300 ft capacity of the WERMAH at about half the typical price, and brass fittings last longer than plastic ones. PU wheels are solid, so they avoid flats like airless tires, though they ride a bit harder on rough ground. It ranks below WERMAH because the connector is not described as a one-piece seam-free part.

Buy it for the capacity at the lowest cost. The listing gives no leader hose detail, so budget for one.
products.idealFor: Large yards on a tighter budget.
products.skipIf: You want a leader hose included.

products.name: VEVOR 250 ft 4-Wheel Hose Reel Cart
products.verdict: Four solid 10 inch PU wheels, brass fittings and a basket for 250 ft of hose.
products.description:
VEVOR's 250 ft cart rolls on four solid 10 inch PU wheels with a powder-coated steel frame, brass fittings, a storage basket and a non-slip handle. It sells for $50 to $100.

The four-wheel layout is stable when you pull, resisting the front-tip that two-wheel carts have. It matches the Poakkus on features but holds 50 ft less, which is why it ranks under it, and it adds no crank detail like Real Hose Storage's foam grip.

Buy it for a mid-size yard with an uneven surface, where solid wheels never go flat. Choose Poakkus if you need the extra 50 ft.

products.name: VEVOR 300 ft 4-Wheel Hose Reel Cart
products.verdict: A heavy-duty powder-coated steel frame for 300 ft, with a wheel-count discrepancy in the listing.
products.description:
VEVOR's 300 ft cart has a heavy-duty powder-coated steel frame, brass fittings, a storage basket and a non-slip handle. It sells for $50 to $100.

The listing is inconsistent on wheels: the title says four, while the description mentions two solid PVC wheels. That matters, because a two-wheel cart tips when pulled and sits unsteadily when a full 300 ft drum is loaded. We rank it below the 250 ft model for that reason, even though capacity is higher.

Buy it only after confirming the wheel count with the seller. If four wheels are confirmed, it is a strong low-cost cart.
products.idealFor: Large yards, once the wheel count is confirmed.
products.skipIf: You cannot verify the wheel layout.

products.name: GrillTown Hosemobile 175 ft Hose Reel Cart
products.verdict: Arrives fully assembled, in resin, with an Easylink watertight connection for 175 ft.
products.description:
The Hosemobile from GrillTown takes 175 ft of 5/8 inch hose. It is shipped already built, molded from resin, and joins the hose with a watertight Easylink coupling. It sells for $50 to $100.

Pre-assembly saves an hour and several lost screws, and the coupling is a clean answer to the leaking connector problem. Resin will not rust, but it is less rigid than steel under a full load. Capacity is the lowest of the cart-style picks, so it ranks last.

Buy it for a small to mid-size yard where setup time matters. Choose steel if you wind a full length often.
products.idealFor: Small yards where fast setup matters.

methodology.title: Connector and fittings
methodology.description: Brass versus plastic and leak design.

whatMatters.detail: Hose capacity is the length of 5/8 inch hose the drum holds, and it sets how heavy the cart gets. A full 300 ft drum is a workout to pull and wind, so more capacity is not free. Count the farthest point you water, add a margin, and match it to the rating: 175 ft for small yards, 250 ft mid-size, 300 ft large lots. Confirm the 5/8 inch hose size in the listing.

Wheel design controls whether the cart tips when you tug the hose. Four wheels spread the load and resist front-tip, while a two-wheel cart pivots forward under a pull. Airless tires like WERMAH's never go flat, and solid PU wheels like Poakkus's are also flat-proof but ride firmer. Check the wheel count in both the title and description, since one VEVOR listing contradicts itself.

The connector joins the hose to the reel, and it is where most carts leak. A one-piece angled brass fitting removes the seam that cheap plastic ones drip from and avoids the kink at the leader. Brass also survives hot sun and freeze cycles. Look for the material by name in the spec list and for a seal claim, and be wary of listings that omit it.

The crank is the part you touch every time, and winding hundreds of feet of wet hose punishes a poor one. A padded ergonomic handle with a smooth gear spreads force across the palm, where a thin bare handle bites. Look for foam grip or ergonomic in the title. Real Hose Storage's E-Z Ergo is the clearest example in this ranking.

Frame material sets how the cart holds up under a full load. Powder-coated steel is stiff, heavy and rust-resistant, while resin, like GrillTown's, will not rust but flexes more when the drum is full. Steel suits long lengths and frequent winding, resin suits a lighter carry and small yards. Check the listing for powder coat or resin and the stated load.

faq.a: All six list 5/8 inch hose, the common garden size, but capacity differs. GrillTown holds 175 ft, Real Hose Storage and VEVOR's smaller cart 250 ft, and WERMAH, Poakkus and VEVOR's larger cart 300 ft. Match it to your longest run.

Choosing by capacity alone. The VEVOR 300 ft listing mixes a four-wheel title with a two-wheel description, and a two-wheel cart tips when you pull. Confirm the wheel count with the seller before buying that one.

faq.q: Is a cart worth it over a wall reel?
faq.a: If you water several areas, yes. A WERMAH or Poakkus rolls the hose to the bed instead of dragging it across the lawn, which saves hose wear and plant damage. For a single spigot and a short run, a wall reel costs less.

faq.q: How do I set it up?
faq.a: Steel carts like Poakkus and VEVOR need assembly, so set aside an hour and keep the parts in a tray. GrillTown arrives fully assembled, and WERMAH includes a 6.5 ft leader hose, so you connect the spigot straight away.

Drain the hose before you wind it, and park the cart out of direct sun, which ages hose and plastic. Brass fittings on WERMAH and Poakkus hold up, and powder-coated frames resist rust. Touch up any chip in the coat.

Yes, both resin and powder-coated steel handle weather. Drain the hose before freezing, because trapped water cracks a connector, and a brass fitting on WERMAH or Poakkus tolerates freeze cycles better than plastic ones do.

finalTake: The WERMAH 300 ft is the hose reel cart to buy if your budget stretches to the top of the range, and Poakkus gives you 300 ft for less. Real Hose Storage wins on crank comfort, and GrillTown suits small yards. Confirm the wheel count and connector before you pay.
